subtopic: JWT Verification, Token Expiration and Revocation Lists
question_text: [Authentication, Authorization & API Security - Q59] Why is stateless JWT validation unable to immediately revoke an individual compromised token without additional backend state?

options.text: Because standard JWT validation relies entirely on cryptographic signature verification against the public key without querying a central database
JWTs can only be decoded by the client
Operating systems cache JWTs in CPU registers

answer_explanation: Stateless tokens are self-contained. Any server with the public key verifies them as valid until their `exp` timestamp, necessitating a distributed blocklist (e.g. Redis) for instant revocation.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Stateless tokens are self-contained. Any server with the public key verifies them as valid until their `exp` timestamp, necessitating a distributed blocklist (e.g. Redis) for instant revocation.
